# Internal-information denylist checked against the WORKING TREE ONLY
# (ci.yml → hygiene job). Companion to .github/internal-terms.txt, which is
# checked against the full history instead.
#
# WHY TWO TIERS
#   internal-terms.txt  → must never exist ANYWHERE, in any blob, in any ref.
#                         Highest impact: customer identity, enterprise identity
#                         and device-compliance plumbing, internal infra names.
#   this file           → must not exist at HEAD, but pre-existing occurrences
#                         are already frozen in public history and cannot be
#                         removed (see below). So this tier only prevents NEW
#                         occurrences from being added.
#
# WHY THE EXISTING OCCURRENCES CANNOT BE REMOVED
#   The term below appears in historical blobs that are reachable from
#   refs/pull/1/head. A pull-request ref tracks its source branch only while
#   that branch exists; once the branch is deleted, GitHub freezes the ref and
#   neither a force-push nor a history rewrite can move it. That ancestry is
#   therefore permanent. Putting the term in the full-history list would make
#   that job unfixably red.
#
#   Operational lesson: when a leak has to be rewritten out of history, do it
#   BEFORE any PR branch that references the affected commits is deleted —
#   force-push the PR branch to a clean equivalent first, so its ref follows.
#
# SELF-REFERENCE TRAP
#   Same convention as the companion file: every pattern is written so it does
#   not literally contain the string it matches (one character in a class), and
#   that applies to comments too. Verify with:
#       PATF=$(mktemp); sed -e 's/#.*//' -e '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' \
#         .github/internal-terms-head-only.txt > "$PATF"
#       grep -inE -f "$PATF" .github/internal-terms-head-only.txt   # must be empty
#
# FORMAT
#   One POSIX extended regex (ERE) per line, case-insensitive.

# ── Product-internal API / call names ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Sensitivity is low (the behaviour is observable by simply using the product's
# UI), but a public sample should describe what the user sees rather than name
# the internal call that causes it. Prefer neutral wording.
register_runtime_[i]ntegration
